solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loses wicket but doesn't declare

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batter who deflects the ball onto their own stumps is out this way
a side that does not declare its innings closed carries on batting

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from cricket: to declare is to end your side's batting innings early by choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cricket idioms: one for being bowled off your own bat, one for continuing to bat rather than closing the innings.

clue.text: It helps an actor to have fun in small part

indicators.note: the word for fun goes in between the letters of the abbreviation for a part

parts.note: PT is the short form of part
a romp is a spell of boisterous fun

explanation.surface: Advice on how an actor can enjoy a minor role.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue whispered from the wings helps an actor who has forgotten a line.

clue.text: A Pole's strangely showing a certain inclination

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word with its S kept

explanation.surface: A Polish person displays some odd leaning or preference.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old adjective meaning sloping, at an angle, so having a tilt.

clue.text: Please try a new version, one at a time

indicators.note: a new version of these words rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A request to have another go at something, perhaps a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things individually rather than together means handling them one at a time.

clue.text: Alan's wrong to be nosy

indicators.note: letters put wrong are set in a different order

parts.note: the letters of the name with its S kept

explanation.surface: Someone named Alan is mistaken in prying into others' affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy here means of the nose, the adjective for sounds or passages of the nose.

clue.text: Whig can get involved in informal chat

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A member of the old Whig party may join in a casual conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were a historical British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial word for a relaxed gossip or natter.

clue.text: Shakespearean role may make actor leap about

explanation.surface: A part in a Shakespeare play could have a performer jumping around the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen is the title character of Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: This nation's rise and fall, in speech

definitions.text: This nation's rise and fall, in speech

parts.words: This nation's rise and fall, in speech
parts.note: put the answer, 'this', before NATION and the result is the rise and fall of the voice in speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer itself: the four letters followed by NATION spell the word for the rise and fall of pitch in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer plus NATION gives the term for voice pitch going up and down, which the clue describes.

clue.text: Risk a wet capsizing to do sport

indicators.note: a capsizing turns things over, so these letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking up a watersport means chancing a soaking if the boat overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over water on skis behind a boat is a sport, so the verb means to do that sport.

clue.text: Assassinate or target revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political choice between murdering a leader or making him the aim of a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone with a wire or cord is a method of killing them.

clue.text: Deck or dock

parts.note: to dock a tail is to lop it, cut it short

explanation.surface: A choice between two nautical places: on deck or in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest deck of a ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Observer Magazine

definitions.meaning: a long-running British weekly political magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is also a British Sunday newspaper, a deliberate misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher at an event is one sense; a British weekly magazine of the same name is the other.

clue.text: They hold the news cuttings together?

definitions.text: They hold the news cuttings together?

parts.words: They hold the news cuttings together?
parts.note: small wire fasteners keep sheets together, and the cuttings from a newspaper could also be called by the same two words

explanation.definitionFit: Small bent wire fasteners keep loose sheets of paper together.

clue.text: Religious instruction's wearing to a small group

indicators.note: RI wearing the word to has it on the outside, so it goes round

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: Religious education is wearing down a small set of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three, such as three musicians, is a small group.

clue.text: A family habit?

parts.note: habit is clothing, as a monk's habit, passed from older to younger children

explanation.definitionFit: Clothes passed down to a younger sibling are a family's shared garments.

clue.text: A case for arms limitation?

parts.note: arms are limbs here, and the case is a garment that pins them, not a disarmament argument

explanation.definitionFit: A restraining garment with long sleeves tied behind confines the wearer's arms.

clue.text: Love a girl, sadly not one to be embraced

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes inside the scrambled word
sadly signals the letters of the word not are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lament: loving a girl, but unhappily not being the one she hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns NOT into TON, and 'to be embraced' puts I inside it to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep devoted affection or worship is a strong synonym for love.

clue.text: Material not to be made light of?

definitions.text: Material not to be made light of?

parts.words: Material not to be made light of?
parts.note: light means set alight: this mineral fibre will not burn, and it is also a health hazard not to take lightly

explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once used for fireproofing will not catch fire.

clue.text: Company lacking any true organising may benefit from one

definitions.text: Company lacking any true organising may benefit from one

indicators.note: the word company is lacking the letters of any, which are taken out
organising the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A firm without real structure would be helped by a modern office machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ANY from COMPANY leaves COMP; 'organising' turns TRUE into UTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm with no system could get organised with a data-processing machine.

clue.text: Stewed pears now sold in ounces

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked into a jumble, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dessert of cooked pears sold by weight in ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounces' looks like weights but is the definition: ounce is another name for a big cat of the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is an alternative name for the pale big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Remove from duty

definitions.meaning: to cut out, as a surgeon does
a tax on goods produced at home

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cut out; the noun is a tax on home-produced goods.

clue.text: Capital for a ship holding company

indicators.note: the ship's letters hold the group word inside them

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a company of people can be called a set

explanation.surface: Money raised for a vessel that a firm owns.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's capital is its holdings of value, its property and resources.

clue.text: Yes! About to grab parking spot

indicators.note: the scrambled word grabs the parking symbol inside it
letters turned about are put in a different order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Joy on finding a parking space in a busy street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns YES into ESY, and 'to grab' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, a synonym for glimpse.

clue.text: The arms of formidable females

parts.note: a weapon used in fighting is also slang for a fierce domineering woman

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy war weapons share their name with slang for overbearing women.

clue.text: Unqualified to sum up

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete and absolute; as a verb it means to add up.

clue.text: Roof party — I object below

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: a do is a party
me is the object form of the pronoun I

explanation.surface: A party protest: someone objects to what is going on underneath the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded vault forms the roof of a building.

clue.text: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients

definitions.text: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients

parts.words: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients
parts.note: skinny means working on skin, and designs are literally put on the clients

explanation.definitionFit: An artist who inks pictures on people's skin puts designs on clients.

clue.text: Think of love and languish

parts.note: O is love, zero in tennis
to pine is to languish, waste away

explanation.surface: Brooding on a lover and wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To state an opinion means to think or hold a view.

clue.text: Swell acting one's seen in the theatre

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea
on means acting, performing on stage

explanation.surface: A fine actor is spotted at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests a stage, but here it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Military dance

explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry regiments with lances are one sense; a nineteenth-century square dance is the other.
